summary: Scenario: RLPlanner (W4390437658), Ascend 910 System, 6 chiplets on a 2.5D interposer. The 2D screening label is illustrative_2d_only, and the Studio run did run (run_kind custom_2d_steady, status completed, run id c9e576d2499d413c90191897c6ed8b9b). The input gate passed with no input errors, so the deterministic gate allowed an exploratory run. The scientific gate failed, independently_verified is false, and comparison_valid is false. Inputs: widths, heights and powers (256, 14, 20, 20, 20, 20 W) come from pinned weiweihook/RLPlanner config/Ascend910.cfg at commit a75abf0b167a316dc5e2dd8b8d3d926114039271. The placement is a generated deterministic shelf layout, not the published RL floorplan, which is unavailable. Units (mm, W) are assumed because the config does not state them. A custom 2D steady run has no transient trace; the input.ptrace is one constant row of source powers, so only a steady-state snapshot is represented. Studio result: with bundled example.materials and package.config, the hottest block was chiplet_1 at 382.38 K (109.23 C). Other chiplets ranged from 88.29 C (chiplet_4) to 98.22 C (chiplet_5). A +1 W perturbation on chiplet_1 raised it to 382.59 K (about +0.21 K), so the model responds plausibly and the sensitivity check passed. Comparison to the paper: the paper's 77.12 C is a system-wide peak for an unpublished RL-optimized placement, with unknown HotSpot or fast-model origin and unknown cooling boundaries. The Studio 109.23 C is a block-level steady temperature for a generated placement under bundled package assumptions. The location, aggregation, placement and boundary assumptions do not match, so the roughly 32 C difference is not a numerical agreement or disagreement and must not be read as replication or refutation. Only qualitative inference is supported: the 256 W chiplet dominates the thermal behavior, and the generated layout, which stacks it next to other chiplets, and the unspecified cooling strongly influence peak temperature. This is an exploratory, illustrative result and not an exact replication of the paper.
limitations: Final RLPlanner chiplet placement coordinates are not published; the shelf layout is generated and illustrative only.

The RL optimizer (PPO plus RND), wirelength, microbump assignment and reward terms are not reproduced by a thermal-only run.
The workload is a single constant-power row; there is no transient trace, power time series or controller, and the Studio run is steady-state only.
Config length and power units (mm, W) are assumed, and chiplet names are index-based only.
The ServeTheHome reference [6] is unpinned and unverified, and the paper gives no repository URL; the pinned config is the only asset evidence.
The scientific gate failed with unresolved adversarial checks, pending independent review and several evidence items lacking valid page or asset locators; comparison_valid is false.
Per-chiplet and temperature-field results are unavailable from the paper, so only the single maximum could be referenced.

The paper's 77.12 degC is a peak temperature for an RL-optimized final placement that is not published, so it cannot be reproduced or numerically compared with a separately generated illustrative placement.

The original thermal evaluation uses HotSpot and an LTI self/mutual-resistance fast model for 2.5D chiplets on an interposer. The interposer, package, heat-spreader and cooling parameters are not given in the paper or pinned config, so the original cooling boundary conditions cannot be matched.

The original method is an RL floorplanner (PPO plus RND) that co-optimizes wirelength and temperature with microbump assignment. A thermal-only Studio run has no optimizer, wirelength or microbump assignment, so that part cannot be replicated.

The paper's workload is a static steady-state power per chiplet, with no transient behaviour, power time series, controller or reliability analysis. Any one-row power trace is a steady-state surrogate only.
The paper's fast thermal model is an LTI approximation with a reported MAE of about 0.25 K vs HotSpot. A different solver will differ in numerical details.
The system is 2.5D (chiplets on an interposer), not 3D stacked, so no vertical stacking mismatch applies. Any Studio 2D model must still represent the interposer layer.
Final chiplet coordinates are not supplied by the reference files; generated shelf positions illustrate a 2D power snapshot, not the published placement.
